method: Refill body 0x18de1e0 run natively with prepare and take hooked as recording services that return a scripted take sequence (30 percent null). The Python reference refill_pose_link_objects runs on copies of the same bytes with the same script; the native lock xadd on 0x14333683c is executed natively and compared against the reference counter.
comparisons: prepare, take and leave call order with arguments (guard value, count, pool value)
every element slot byte, including null slots and slots beyond the count
every constructed object byte range 0x100 including unused slack
final serial global value against the reference counter
coverage: null take at random positions, all null, none null

limits: Protected prepare thunk and the pool take are supplied services; their memory effects are not modeled and not validated.
The pool take slow path (0x18b5d35) is not reconstructed, so the pool free-list state is not validated beyond the script.
The native pool global is read once per pass in the model; the native code re-reads it. No service in the harness writes it.
The native take result is not checked for lifetime; the harness assumes the taken object is writable for 0x100 bytes.
No live validation, no concurrent refill, no pool exhaustion behavior beyond null takes.
